# `@` — At

`A@I Y` replaces selected items with `A`, returning a new array.

```bpl
0@1 3 ⍳5           ⍝ 0 0 2 0 4
```

`f@I Y` applies `f` to the selection, then puts it back.

```bpl
⌽@1 3 ⍳5           ⍝ 0 3 2 1 4
```

Numeric index arrays select leading-axis cells. Their shape precedes the remaining cell axes, as with [Index](squad.qmd) `⌷`.

```bpl
v←10 20 30 40 ⋄ i←[0 3 ⋄ 1 2]
{⍵+[100 200 ⋄ 300 400]}@i v   ⍝ 110 320 430 240
```

A function right operand computes a Boolean selection mask.

```bpl
0@ 2| ⍳5          ⍝ 0 0 2 0 4
```

A keyed replacement aligns by key with the selected positions, as it does in assignment.

```bpl
x←["a":1 "b":2 "c":3]
["b":20 "a":10]@0 1 x   ⍝ ["a":10 "b":20 "c":3]
```

Indices include nested paths. Dyadic calls pass the left argument to the replacement function. Repeated indices are written in order; the last replacement wins.
